CHEMISTRY — MOCK EXAM #14
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: CHEMISTRY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Primary consumers only

2. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. watt (W)
   C. joule (J)
   D. newton (N)

3. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water always increases oxygen

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Mole? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Mole.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Mole.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on The Mole.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Mole.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Salts ● Action of heat on salts (carbonates and hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, a? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Salts ● Action of heat on salts (carbonates and hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, a.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Salts ● Action of heat on salts (carbonates and hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, a.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Salts ● Action of heat on salts (carbonates and hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, a.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Salts ● Action of heat on salts (carbonates and hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, a.

7. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 50 °C

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.

9. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

10. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Removing all vegetation

11. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.

13. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only carbon dioxide

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.

15. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Heating until a solid melts

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.

17. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.

18. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Milk souring
   D. Iron rusting

19. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
20. In three clear sentences, explain Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
